intent.name: finance.budget.prepare
intent.summary: Prepare a budget for a financial period, line by line, with last period's actuals offered as a starting point. One step, and it controls nothing yet.
routesHere: prepare the budget for FY 2026-27 by department

routesHere.text: agle saal ka budget bana do
har department ka budget alag rakho

routesHere: draft the budget by account for the coming period

routesElsewhere.note: Figures cannot be changed after approval except through a recorded revision (BR-3).
Actuals are read from the ledger, never entered against the budget by hand (BR-4).

request.text: is voucher ko rok do, budget se zyada hai
request.gloss: block this voucher, it is over budget

routesElsewhere.note: The budget is a reference with a warning, not a hard control. A voucher exceeding its line is flagged and pushed up a level, never blocked (BR-1, BR-2).

steps.note: One step, producing a Draft. Nothing is written to the ledger — a budget is a plan set alongside the books, not part of them (BR-9).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A missing chart of accounts, an undefined financial year, departments chosen where none exist, a negative figure and a budget that already exists for the period are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the budget and all its lines together with the audit entry, or not at all. Nothing in the ledger is touched (BR-9). It is a Draft, so no voucher consumes it and no variance is reported against it yet.

operations.name: finance.budget.prepare
operations.idempotencyKey: period + scope + branch_id, since one budget exists per period
operations.purpose: Create a draft budget for a period, with a figure against each account or department.

parameters.name: period
parameters.notes: The financial period the budget covers. Not the academic session — the financial year is a different thing and is defined nowhere in the specification (BR-12, E2).

parameters.name: scope
parameters.notes: Whether the budget is prepared by account or by department. Departments must exist where that scope is chosen (E3).

parameters.name: lines
parameters.notes: One entry per account or department, each with a budgeted amount of zero or more (E4) and optionally a note on what the figure assumes. Every figure comes from the request — last period's actual is offered as a starting point, not applied as one.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Draft. No voucher consumes it and no variance is reported yet.

fields.name: financial_year
fields.description: The year it runs against, which is not the academic session (BR-12).

errors.note: No feature in the specification creates one (BR-12).
Also defined nowhere in the specification (BR-12).

errors.meaning: Departments were chosen as the scope but none exist.
errors.note: Prepare it by account instead, which is the actor's decision (A5).

errors.meaning: A budget already exists for the period.
errors.note: The message names it. Changing it is a revision, not a second budget (BR-3).

planningRules.rule: Never carry last period's actual into a figure. It is offered as a starting point, not applied as one — a budget that repeats what happened is a forecast nobody made.
Never supply a figure the request did not state. A budget is what somebody is measured against (BR-8), and a number a planner filled in measures them against nothing they agreed.
Never describe the budget as controlling spend. It is a reference with a warning, not a hard control — a voucher exceeding its line is flagged and pushed up a level, never blocked (BR-1, BR-2).
Never confuse the financial period with the academic session. They are different, and the financial year is defined nowhere in the specification (BR-12).
Never create a second budget for a period. E8 means one exists; changing it is a recorded revision, because a budget anybody can quietly replace measures nothing (BR-3).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A draft is not deleted — the lifecycle runs Draft, Awaiting approval, Approved, Revised, Returned, Closed. An unwanted draft is simply not approved. After approval, figures change only through a recorded revision (BR-3).

request.text: FY 2026-27 ka budget bana do, department ke hisab se
request.gloss: prepare the FY 2026-27 budget, by department

resolvedPlans.outcome: A Draft with a line per department and last period's actual shown against each. Nothing is written to the ledger (BR-9) and no voucher consumes it until it is approved.

intent.name: finance.budget.approve
intent.summary: Approve a budget so vouchers begin consuming its lines and variance is reported against it. One step.

routesElsewhere.note: An approved budget is not edited directly (BR-3, E6).

steps.note: One step. From here approved but unpaid vouchers consume their lines, so a commitment is visible before the money leaves (BR-5), and variance is reported against both the original and any revised figure (BR-7).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Nothing in the ledger is written by this (BR-9).
plan.atomicity: One write: the approval and the audit entry together or not at all. Nothing in the ledger changes — a budget is a plan set alongside the books, not part of them (BR-9). From here the figures cannot be changed except through a recorded revision (BR-3), actuals accumulate from the ledger as the period progresses (BR-4), and approved but unpaid vouchers consume their lines so a commitment is visible before the money leaves (BR-5).

operations.name: finance.budget.approve
operations.idempotencyKey: budget_id + version, since a budget version carries one approval
operations.purpose: Approve a budget so vouchers consume it and variance is reported against it.

parameters.name: budget_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No budget matches at a status that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with period, scope, status and version.

parameters.notes: The budget, resolved from how the actor named it — the period, or simply the current one.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: version
fields.description: 1 on first approval; incremented on each approved revision (BR-6).

fields.name: ledger_entries_written
fields.description: Always zero. Nothing in the ledger is written by this use case (BR-9).

errors.meaning: An approved budget was edited directly.
errors.note: Changes are made as a recorded revision (BR-3).

planningRules.rule: Never describe approval as writing to the books. Nothing in the ledger is written by this use case — a budget is a plan set alongside the books, not part of them (BR-9).
Report that figures are now fixed except by revision. A budget anybody can quietly edit measures nothing (BR-3), and the revision leaves a reason and a version behind (BR-6).

Report that approved but unpaid vouchers will consume the lines. A budget counting only paid invoices reports last month rather than this one (BR-5), and a commitment is visible before the money leaves.
Never chain a revision onto an approval. Approving the figures somebody prepared and then changing them is not two acts, it is one act pretending to be two.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: An approved budget is not unapproved. Figures change only through a recorded revision with its author, date and reason, and previous versions stay readable (BR-3, BR-6). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

request.text: FY 2026-27 ka budget approve kar do

resolvedPlans.outcome: Approved at version 1. Actuals now accumulate from the ledger, and approved but unpaid vouchers consume their lines so a commitment shows before the money leaves (PR-3). Nothing was written to the ledger (PR-1).

request.text: budget approve kar do aur utilities ka figure bhi barha do
request.gloss: approve the budget and raise the utilities figure too

steps.note: Only the approval is planned. Changing a figure after approval is a recorded revision (PR-4).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Approved as prepared. Report that raising utilities is a separate revision with its own reason — approving figures and then changing them in the same breath is one act pretending to be two.

request.gloss: change utilities to 500,000 in the budget

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, on an already approved budget.

steps.note: Emitted as an approval; the API returns EDIT_AFTER_APPROVAL (E6) for a direct edit.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing changes. Report that an approved budget is revised, not edited — and that a revision carries a reason, because a figure moved without explanation makes variance meaningless (PR-2).

intent.name: finance.budget.revise
intent.summary: Revise an approved budget figure, with the reason it moved, keeping the original readable. One step.
routesHere: revise the utilities line up to 500,000 — tariffs rose

routesHere.text: utilities ka budget barha do, bijli mehngi ho gayi
routesHere.gloss: raise the utilities budget, electricity has become expensive

routesHere.text: transport ka figure kam kar do

routesHere: revise the salaries line, we've hired two more teachers

routesElsewhere.note: One budget exists per period (E8); changing it is a revision.

steps.note: One step. The revision is recorded with its author, date and reason, and previous versions stay readable — a figure moved without explanation makes variance meaningless (BR-6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A missing reason and a negative figure are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the new figures, the reason, the incremented version and the audit entry together or not at all. Nothing in the ledger changes (BR-9). Earlier versions stay readable, and variance is afterwards reported against **both** the original and the revised figure — because variance against a figure revised upward mid-year looks healthy while the original tells the real story (BR-7).

operations.name: finance.budget.revise
operations.idempotencyKey: budget_id + version + the revision set, so a repeat does not increment the version twice
operations.purpose: Revise one or more approved budget lines, recording the reason and incrementing the version.

parameters.name: budget_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No budget matches at a status that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with period, scope, status and version.

parameters.notes: The budget, resolved from how the actor named it — the period, or simply the current one.

parameters.name: revisions
parameters.notes: The lines to change and their new figures, each zero or more (E4). Only the lines the request changes — a line not named keeps its figure.

parameters.name: revision_reason
parameters.notes: 20 to 500 characters. Required for every revision (BR-6, E5), since a figure moved without explanation makes variance meaningless. The actor's own words.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The revision, and what it replaced.

fields.name: revision_reason
fields.description: As given, kept with the version.

fields.name: original_total
fields.description: The figure first approved, which is what tells the real story (BR-7).

errors.meaning: A revision was made with no reason.
errors.note: Message: "Give a reason. A figure moved without explanation makes variance meaningless." Ask; never compose one.

errors.meaning: A budget holder attempted to change their own line.
errors.note: Somebody who can move the figure they are measured against is not being measured (BR-8).

planningRules.rule: Never compose the revision reason. A figure moved without explanation makes variance meaningless (BR-6), and the reason is what somebody reads when the variance looks healthy and the original figure does not.
Revise only the lines the request names. A line not mentioned keeps its figure, and restating the whole budget records revisions nobody made.

Never revise a line to accommodate an overspend. The budget is a reference with a warning; a voucher over its line is escalated, not blocked (BR-1, BR-2), and moving the figure afterwards makes the escalation look like it never happened.

Report both totals. Variance is shown against the original and the revised figure, because variance against a figure revised upward mid-year looks healthy while the original tells the real story (BR-7).
Never revise on a budget holder's behalf. Somebody who can move the figure they are measured against is not being measured (BR-8, E7).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A revision is not undone. Revising back is another revision with its own reason, and every version stays readable (BR-6). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

operations.name: finance.budget.variance.read
operations.purpose: Return each budget line with its budgeted, committed and actual figures, and the variance against both the original and any revised figure.

parameters.name: budget_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No budget matches at a status that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with period, scope, status and version.

parameters.notes: The budget, resolved from how the actor named it — the period, or simply the current one.

parameters.name: line_id
parameters.notes: One line, where the request names one. Omitted for the whole budget.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: Where the plan and the books stand against each other.

fields.name: lines
fields.description: account_or_department, budgeted_original, budgeted_revised, committed, actual, variance_to_original, variance_to_revised.

fields.name: committed
fields.description: Approved but unpaid vouchers, so a commitment is visible before the money leaves (BR-5).

fields.name: actual
fields.description: Read from the ledger. Never entered by hand (BR-4).

fields.name: variance_to_original
fields.description: Against the figure first approved, which is what tells the real story (BR-7).

fields.name: variance_to_revised
fields.description: Against the current revised figure, where one exists (BR-7).

fields.name: over_budget_lines
fields.description: Lines where actual plus committed exceeds the figure. Flagged, never blocking (BR-1).

errors.meaning: An actual figure was entered by hand against the budget.
errors.note: Actuals are read from the ledger (BR-4). There is no parameter for one here.

planningRules.rule: Never compute an actual or a variance. Actuals are read from the ledger and never entered by hand (BR-4), and a figure worked out in a reply is a number nobody can trace to the books.

Report variance against both figures, always. Variance against a line revised upward mid-year looks healthy while the original tells the real story (BR-7) — reporting only the revised one flatters the position.
Report committed separately from actual. An approved but unpaid voucher consumes the line, and a budget counting only what has been paid reports last month rather than this one (BR-5).
Never describe an over-budget line as blocked. The budget is a reference with a warning — a voucher exceeding its line is flagged and pushed up a level, never refused (BR-1, BR-2).
A budget holder reads their own variance and cannot change it (BR-8). Never offer them a revision.

operations.name: finance.budget.return
operations.purpose: Send a prepared budget back with the reason it was not approved.

parameters.name: budget_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No budget matches at a status that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with period, scope, status and version.

parameters.notes: The budget, resolved from how the actor named it — the period, or simply the current one.

parameters.name: return_reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Required. The approver's own words — which lines are wrong and why.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Returned. The period has no approved budget.

errors.meaning: A return was recorded with no reason.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the return reason. Which lines are wrong and why is exactly what the preparer needs, and a general objection sends them back to guess.
Report that the period has no approved budget. Until one is approved, no line is consumed and no variance is reported — the office is spending against nothing (BR-1, BR-5).
Never adjust a figure on the approver's behalf.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A return is not undone. The budget is corrected and submitted again, which is a fresh decision.
